newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Motor racing-Melbourne transport strike a "disaster".
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Motor racing-Melbourne transport strike a "disaster".

text.p: Australia Grand Prix boss Ron Walker said on Thursday a planned strike by public transport workers in the city this weekend would create a financial disaster by causing a drop in the race attendance on Sunday.
Walker said the absence of buses, trains and trams would deter spectators from travelling to Albert Park for the season-opening Formula One race and cost the city millions of dollars in lost revenue.
"It's ruined us as far as the (organising) Grand Prix Corporation is concerned. It will cost the taxpayers millions of dollars and it's bad for our international reputation," Walker said.

Walker made his comments after public transport workers in Australia's second city voted to stage a 48-hour strike, starting at midnight on Friday, in pursuit of a wage claim and better working condtions.
More than 400,000 fans over four days attended the Australian Grand Prix last year when it was staged at the inner-city street circuit for the first time.
The strike action is the latest development in a dispute between the local transport workers' union and the Victoria state government.
